mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.75% over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%, or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals improved consumer purchasing power, which boosts demand and supports higher corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-average payroll employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 6-month averages signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall below 6-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST are below their 6-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent drop in the unemployment rate to below 5% for three consecutive months in a late-cycle context signals labor market overheating, which increases wage pressures and inflation risk, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as discount rates rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for 3 consecutive months in late cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when unemployment falls below 5% for three consecutive months in a late-cycle environment.
